method_notes.A: Primary tokenizer: lowercase, curly apostrophes -> ', words = [a-z]+ with internal apostrophes; hyphens split words; dictionary terms tokenized the same way and matched as contiguous phrases (no wildcards exist in either .dic file). Variants in motif_scoring_summary.json.
method_notes.B: Unit share = flagged/all present motifs. Country incidence values are continuous population-weighted fractions (row sums = motifs_total), not counts. Both weighted and unweighted shares were computed; expected numbers reproduce only with incidence-weighted shares. EA incidence is 0/1 (two cells = 2). 8 incidence columns carry a trailing underscore (b28e_, d4aa_, e15_, e15a_, e15b_, e18_, h36g1_, m81_) and were mapped back to their motif ids. Units with <5 motifs dropped (0 countries, 31 EA groups) before z-scoring.
method_notes.p_values: Mine use Stata conventions: HC1 with t(N-K); clustered with t(G-1). Original uses statsmodels normal-based p-values, which explains small p differences.

A_motif_scoring.claim: share of motifs with >=1 virtue term

A_motif_scoring.note: 14.47% if hyphenated words are kept as single tokens (then 'daughter-in-law' no longer matches 'in law').
Difference is one motif (m30b, 'give and take back'): matched by the dictionary's 'give-and-take' only when hyphenated terms are split into phrases.

A_motif_scoring.what_matters: (1) hyphen handling: splitting 'daughter-in-law' lets it match 'in law' (Family); (2) apostrophe handling: keeping "partner's" as one token stops it matching 'partner' (Group); (3) the original's extra -est/-eth stemmer ('noblest'->'noble', Heroism). Only 4 of 2,564 motifs differ from the original's flags, but because the 7 domains are equally weighted and some are near-empty (Fairness 2 motifs, Deference 9), those 4 flips move the EA estimate from 0.071 to 0.077.

original_code_review.issue: unit_scores keeps only incidence columns whose names are in the flag index, silently dropping 8 motifs whose incidence columns end in '_' (b28e_, d4aa_, e15_, e15a_, e15b_, e18_, h36g1_, m81_; d4aa is a vice-Property motif). Wrong merge key; effect tiny (EA 0.0776 -> 0.0771, WVS -0.0226 -> -0.0221).

Country shares are weighted by the fractional population-weighted incidence; the stated rule says weight only if the file has counts. The expected values depend on this choice (unweighted: WVS -0.09, GPS +0.03). Weighting is defensible (README: unweighted presence picks up border slivers), but it should be stated.

The S2-2 claim cites the cont0 results (no individual controls), but describes the model as following the do-file's individual controls. The cont1 results (+0.015; CCI_net +0.036, p=0.002; trickster 1.07, p=0.008) are the ones matching that description. Code is otherwise equivalent to the do-file (rel, health, gender, age deciles verified identical).

C(cntry_round) dummies in OLS keep 4 singleton observations that reghdfe drops (n 6,558/117 vs 6,554/116). p-values here and at lines 52 and 76 use a normal reference, not Stata's t(N-K) or t(G-1): slightly smaller p.

Dictionary keys split on whitespace only, but the text tokenizer splits on hyphens, so all 43 hyphenated dictionary terms ('in-law', 'mother-in-law', 'give-and-take', 'self-denial', 'even-handed', ...) and 'i.o.u.' can never match.
An unstated -est/-eth stemmer adds matches the described method would not ('noblest' -> 'noble'). Together with the hyphen issue this changes 4 motif flags.
pd.cut bins are right-closed, so year -500 falls in 'pre500BCE' though the spec says 'before -500'. No crisis sits exactly on -500 or 1500, so there is no effect. Same at h8_3_population.py line 15.

No coding errors found. Coding, severity min_count=2, removed=max, MERb, era fallback and polity clustering match the spec. The crisis 'polity' key matches the frame and covariate ids (169/169; names agree in 151, the rest are spelling variants). The PolPop omission was a coding slip; h8_3_population.py fixes it and reproduces exactly.
